**Analysis Summary:**

- Stem at the crown/soil line — classic location for soil-borne pathogens
- Completely bleached/white-gray cortex tissue — dry, papery, killed tissue
- Small dark round sclerotia (black) on the stem surface
- Healthy green stem above the lesion, dead tissue only at soil contact zone

**Reference comparison:**
- Southern_Blight Bugwood_13: Same black plastic mulch context, collapsed plants — matches field setting

- Southern_Blight Bugwood_19: Uprooted plant showing bleached cortex throughout crown/root zone — matches the dry bleached texture

**Diagnosis:** The combination of (1) bleached cortex tissue precisely at the soil line, (2) small round dark sclerotia on the stem surface (characteristic mustard-seed-sized sclerotia of *Sclerotium rolfsii*), and (3) the crown-specific attack pattern strongly points to **Southern Blight**. Sclerotinia would have larger, internal sclerotia and a more watery initial rot, not this dry bleached cortex with external sclerotia.
